rationale.text: The test forbids presentation attributes in the generated source, and the methodology lists them, with two exceptions: size on select, and width and height on img, object, embed, canvas and svg. Whether an element carries an attribute is a fact of the DOM, so the entry can be full. The wording is about presence in the generated source, so hidden elements count, as in 10.1.1. The custom check faults the page when an HTML element of the top-level document, outside shadow trees, carries a listed attribute that HTML 4.01 or the current HTML standard defines for that element (align on div or td, bgcolor on body, border on table or img, frameborder on iframe, size on input or hr, width on td or table, and so on), other than on the excepted elements. Restricting faults to those defined pairs keeps the witness surely in scope: there the attribute is the presentational attribute the RGAA list names, so a fault proves failure. It abstains where a reader could disagree: the same name on an element that defines no such attribute (a custom element's size or color property, a data-like size on a div); color on a link element, used for a pinned-tab icon; width or height on iframe, video, input or source, which the HTML standard treats as dimension attributes of embedded content like those of the excepted elements, though the RGAA list does not name them; attributes on SVG or MathML elements other than the svg element's own width and height, which are geometry, not HTML presentation; a listed name carried in a namespace; a case variant of a listed name, such as ALIGN in an XHTML document (application/xhtml+xml), where names are case-sensitive and ALIGN is not the align attribute, as Codex's re-check showed in Chrome (HTML parsing lower-cases names, so ordinary HTML pages are unaffected, and the check compares every attribute and element name exactly); listed attributes in shadow trees, framed documents, template content or noscript text, and any of these it cannot read. It also abstains when an HTML element carries one of the other presentational attributes the HTML standard lists as obsolete but RGAA does not name, such as nowrap, face, bordercolor or scrolling: the methodology validates the test once its list is absent, and the abstention is a margin against a broader reading of the wording. The check states its order of decision, since some abstained pairs (width on iframe or video, color on link) are defined by the HTML standard and would otherwise also meet the fault rule. First the fault: any defined pair outside the two exceptions and outside the abstained pairs, on any element of the top-level document, hidden or not, faults the page, and a fault wins over every exception and every abstention the page also holds, so a page with an excepted img width and a td width fails. Then cannot_tell, when there is no fault and the page holds an abstained case. Otherwise no_fault for the whole document, which includes a page whose only listed attributes are on the excepted elements. Hidden instances are treated the same way in all three steps, since the test is about presence in the source. The route and both exceptions can each come out passed. The link is resolving and its fault means failure. No axe rule is tagged. Applicability is always: the test applies to every page, and the check never answers inapplicable. Needs is empty.
